answer: Palm-vein enrollment, the Amazon One approach, ties each agent to one living hand. First, the operator hovers a palm over a kiosk, light as a whisper, while near-infrared light maps the veins beneath the skin. Second, the template is hashed and checked against every enrolled palm; a near-match is rejected. Third, the agent key is signed to that hash, renewed by a re-scan every 90 days. A farm of 1,000 keys needs 1,000 real people at $25 each plus travel, near $40,000 and six weeks of recruiting. It's a saffron harvest: every thread is picked by hand, and no zephyr blows in a free crop.
